lesson.menu_title: What the Teacher Said — Passing on Messages Without Losing Them
lesson.menu_desc: Relaying instructions, fixing misunderstandings and reporting what people said -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- What the Teacher Said: Passing on Messages Without Losing Them
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Laís Paludetto Rodrigues | Lesson 7 -- What the Teacher Said

listenings.text: Lais, sorry, I'm catching you between classes so I'll be quick, and could you pass this on to the rest of your group? The presentation has been moved to Thursday, not Wednesday, because the hall is being used for the assembly. Tell them they still have to send me the slides on Tuesday evening, that part has not changed. Also, remind Owen that he owes me his source list, he knows what I mean. And warn them that the room is smaller, so if they were planning anything with a big screen, it will not work. That is everything. Thank you, and sorry for the ambush.

Hey, it's Dylan. Okay so I heard from someone that the presentation got moved and honestly I'm not sure I understood it right. Somebody said Thursday, somebody else said the slides were cancelled, and now everyone in the group chat is saying different things. Did she actually say Thursday, or did she say we have to send everything by Thursday? Because those are extremely different. Also apparently there's something about the room and a screen and nobody knows what that means. Could you just tell me exactly what she said, word for word if you can? I'd rather double-check now than turn up on the wrong day, honestly.

extra_audio.text: The teacher stops Lais in the corridor and gives her four things to pass on. Lais writes them down before she forgets. In the group chat somebody says the presentation was cancelled. Dylan asks Lais to repeat exactly what the teacher said. Lais reports the four points in order and the misunderstanding is sorted out.

items.situation: The teacher told you the presentation is on Thursday. Report it to your group.
tips: She said the presentation was on Thursday.
She told us the hall was being used.
The slides are still due on Tuesday.

items.situation: Somebody in the group chat has spread a wrong version. Correct it without blaming anybody.
tips: I think there's been a misunderstanding.
I wrote it down, so I'm sure about this part.

items.situation: Your host mum asked you to be home by nine and you need to tell your friend why you are leaving.
tips: She asked me to be home by nine.
She told me to text if I was going to be late.
It's not a punishment, it's just the rule.

items.situation: A teacher asked you a question in class and you did not catch it. Ask her to repeat it, and then repeat it back to check.
tips: Sorry, could you say that again?
So you're asking whether we finished the reading?

items.situation: You promised to pass on a message and you forgot for two days. Apologise and deliver it now.
tips: I'm really sorry, I completely forgot.
She asked me to tell you that...
It's still fine, the deadline is Friday.

items.situation: Somebody says you said something you never said. Sort it out calmly.
tips: I think we misunderstood each other.
